text: Recommendations for integrating the local-models suite with Claude as a cheap, always-available, DECOUPLED worker fleet (vs cloud Claude sub-agents: tokens + session-coupled + throttle-prone). Target = real recurring multi-step work (isolated-worktree PR review; OOM-log triage -> write+run a local repro/profiler -> code ready to commit), NOT throwaway one-shots. Integration ladder, cheapest first: (1) shell-tool - Claude runs review-pr/see/q via Bash (works today, zero infra); (2) a Claude subagent wrapping the suite; (3) an MCP server exposing see/review/q as native tools (also serves the better-file-browser extension); (4) docs/07 Phase-1 Procedures with qwen3.6 as worker + a Judge gate (now justified: Task #8 gate GREEN, qwen3.6 9/9). PR-review design: orchestrator (Claude/deterministic script, NOT the local model per docs/03) makes the tool calls - git worktree add (main tree untouched) -> gh pr view/diff -> read full changed files -> q review (code tier) -> worktree remove. Local fleet fits HIGH-VOLUME, LOW-STAKES-PER-CALL, VERIFIABLE work (review, recon, homework-checking, mechanical transforms) where cost + availability beat peak intelligence; Claude keeps hard reasoning/design/synthesis. Open question in progress: direct-calls vs Claude-called vs mix, and the ratio.
